title: The referee's lad
summary: The referee's son, the one you signed a shirt for, is a referee himself now. Tonight he's in the middle of your game, his first in the league, and his dad is in the stand.

ends.title: A good game
ends.text: The referee's son refereed your game and got every big call right. His dad framed the team sheet.

ends.title: The big call
ends.text: The referee's son gave a penalty against you in his first game. It was right. You told him so.

beats.title: The tunnel

event.title: The tunnel
event.speaker: referee
setup: In the tunnel the referee is twenty-three, very nervous and very tidy. You signed a shirt for him when he was a boy. He doesn't mention it, so you can tell he's thinking about it.

say: His dad, {referee.short}, is in the main stand in a suit, holding his programme with both hands.

replies.label: Say nothing. Let him do his job.

wish.text: He nods. In the seventy-first minute he gives a penalty against you, and it's right.

shirt.text: He goes red. "In a frame." Then he books you for a late one in the first half and doesn't look sorry.

quiet.text: He has a good game. You don't notice him once, which is the best thing you can say about a referee.

beats.hint: The referee's son is refereeing your game

beats.title: His letter

event.title: His letter
event.speaker: referee
setup: A season on. A letter from {referee.short}, the dad, on headed paper from the referees' society.

outcomes.text: "He said you shook his hand after he gave the penalty. He talks about it at every course."
"He's on the list for the top league now. He says you were the first to wish him luck."
You read it a week later: his son is on the top list. The team sheet from that night is framed in their hall.
You read it a week later. The penalty was right, and the lad still thinks about your handshake.

beats.hint: A season on, a letter from the referee
